headline: Recalling the moment he was shot
summary: In a letter to his friend William Sturgis Bigelow, Roosevelt describes the Milwaukee shooting: stepping into the car from a bright hotel, telling the crowd not to hurt the gunman, and feeling almost no pain beyond his broken rib.

tr_quotes.text: I was getting into the barouche, having just left a lighted hotel, so that I could not see the ground distinctly. What I said when the man was caught was: 'Don't hurt him. Bring him here. I want to look at him.' After the bullet I had no real pain. The wound felt hot . . . When I began to speak my heart beat rapidly for some ten minutes but aside from that about all the real trouble I had was that on account of my broken rib.
